title: Lessons Learned from Developing a Web-Based Platform for Complex Simulation Systems: Software Quality in Distributed Service Architectures
content: The increasing complexity of defense and aerospace computational environments has driven the adoption of scalable, service-oriented architectures supporting collaborative and multi-user operations. This shift is reinforced by innovation policies promoting shared infrastructures across government, academia, and industry. Within this scope, this work proposes a participatory evaluation of the SIMaaS platform for simulation services in the Brazilian Air Force, based on Participatory Research Methodology (PRM) and software and systems engineering criteria. Continuous interaction between developers and end users enabled iterative requirements refinement and progressive system validation throughout the lifecycle. Results indicate improved scalability, interoperability, and collaborative use, as well as reduced learning effort through consistent abstraction of operational complexity across user profiles. In heterogeneous defense, engineering, and research contexts, the framework enhances usability through a unified conceptual model. Key lessons highlight that sustained domain participation is essential for requirements consistency, while iterative engineering and modular architectures improve adaptability, system evolution, and interoperability in complex simulation environments.
